name: LahLah Voice
subtitle: Say what you mean, in any app
keywords: dictation,voice typing,speech to text,keyboard,transcribe,voice notes,filler words,on device
promotional_text: Talk naturally and get finished text. LahLah Voice removes the ums, follows your corrections and writes what you meant, privately on your iPhone.
description:
Talk the way you think. LahLah Voice writes what you meant.

Most dictation types every um, restart and change of mind. LahLah Voice understands them. Say "let's meet Tuesday, no wait, Wednesday" and you get "Let's meet Wednesday." Say "first the budget, second the timeline" and you get a numbered list.

WORKS WHERE YOU WRITE
The LahLah Voice keyboard works in messaging apps, email, notes, AI assistants and any other app with a text field. Tap Speak, talk, tap again, and your text appears.

UNDERSTANDS WHAT YOU MEANT
- Removes pause fillers, stutters and false starts
- Follows spoken corrections such as "no wait", "actually" and "scratch that"
- Fixes punctuation and capitalisation
- Formats spoken lists
- Adjusts your tone: polished, casual, very casual or enthusiastic

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Speech recognition and editing run on your iPhone using Apple Intelligence and Apple's on-device speech recognition. There's no account, no server, no tracking and no advertising.

MAKE IT YOURS
- Dictionary: names and jargon, spelled your way
- Snippets: say a short cue to insert a link, address or common reply
- Voice notes: record a thought or meeting, then get a summary and action items
- History: see what you said next to what was written, stored only on your device

START FROM ANYWHERE
Open a voice session from the app, Control Center, the Action button or Siri. A Live Activity shows when the session is open, and it closes by itself when idle.

REQUIREMENTS
Requires iOS 26 or later. Understanding what you meant and tone changes use Apple Intelligence on supported iPhones. On other iPhones, LahLah Voice still removes fillers and applies spoken corrections using built-in rules. Dictating from the keyboard requires Full Access, which only lets the keyboard reach the LahLah Voice app on your iPhone. Typing works without it.
review_notes:
LahLah Voice is a dictation keyboard. No account or sign-in is needed.

TO TEST IN THE APP (simplest): On the Home tab, tap Speak under "Try it here", allow the microphone, and say "um let's meet on Tuesday no wait Wednesday". Tap Done. The text reads "Let's meet on Wednesday." The first run may download Apple's on-device speech model.

TO TEST THE KEYBOARD: In Settings, go to General > Keyboard > Keyboards > Add New Keyboard > LahLah Voice, then tap LahLah Voice and turn on Allow Full Access. In LahLah Voice, tap Start voice session. Open Notes or Messages, switch to the LahLah Voice keyboard with the globe key, tap Speak, talk, and tap again.

WHY THE KEYBOARD WORKS THIS WAY: iOS keyboard extensions cannot use the microphone, so the containing app holds the audio session in the background (UIBackgroundModes: audio). This is shown by a Live Activity and the system microphone indicator. Audio between dictations is discarded immediately, and the session closes itself after a user-chosen idle time. The keyboard does not launch other apps. If no session is open, it explains how to start one.

GUIDELINE 4.4.1: The keyboard is a full typing keyboard, works without Full Access and without network access, and has a next-keyboard key. Full Access is used only for the App Group that connects the keyboard to the containing app.

PRIVACY: Speech recognition and editing are on-device (SpeechAnalyzer and Foundation Models). The app has no servers, analytics or tracking.

APPLE INTELLIGENCE: On devices without Apple Intelligence, the app uses built-in rules for fillers and corrections.
